Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
308 AM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 229 AM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 308 AM EDT Thursday...

3. The highest probability (45%-65%) of rain showers in the 
extended period will be on Tuesday/Tuesday Night, but no 
significant impacts expected. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 308 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 3: A progressive west to east pattern is progged to be acrs 
our cwa for days 4 thru 7, supporting a boundary every couple of 
days with near normal temps. The deepest moisture and best 
instability looks to be mostly south of our cwa, but pw values 1.60-
1.90" ahead of boundary on Tuesday with some weak instability wl 
produce a band of showers, similar to what we experienced on Weds 
evening. Given sfc based CAPE values btwn 250-400 J/kg, the 
probability of severe is <10% attm. The llvl gradient strengthens 
ahead of approaching cold frnt with progged 850mb winds of 30 to 45 
knots, supporting localized gusts 25 to 40 mph, especially summits 
and Lake Champlain. Progged 925mb temps warm btwn 17-20C Tues/Weds, 
supporting highs well into the 70s with a few lower 80s possible in 
the warmer valleys if some sunshine develops on southwest downslope 
flow. A deeper/sharper mid/upper lvl trof and associated low pres is 
progged to develop acrs the Mid Atlantic/SNE Coast by late next 
week. Still plenty of uncertainty on placement/track of sfc low pres 
and if any moisture can spread this farther north. For now WPC has 
some chc pops on Thurs. Temps cool back into the mid 60s to mid 70s 
for Weds/Thurs with lows near 40F SLK to lower/mid 50s near Lake 
Champlain for midweek.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 06Z Friday...Current radar is showing rain showers
exiting the Champlain Valley and should be thru MPV and EFK in
the next 1 to 2 hours. Currently a mix of MVFR/VFR, which should
trend toward VFR by 12z this morning as much drier air aloft
builds across our taf sites. Winds continue from the
south/southwest 5 to 10 knots with localized gusts 10 to 20
knots this morning, but shift to the northwest at similar speeds
by noon-time today. Another weak system will produce more clouds
and maybe a few showers this evening, with some MVFR cigs
possible at EFK and SLK toward sunset. 

Outlook...

Friday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Friday Night: VFR. Patchy BR.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
Southwesterly wind gusts 10 to 15 knots are expected on Lake 
Champlain this morning, becoming northwesterly 15 to 20 knots
with gusts around 25 knots this afternoon. Waves will be around
1 to 3 feet today. Winds will become weaker tonight around 5 to
15 knots out of the northwest.

&&
